name: The she-wolf, walking north
stands_for: The she-wolf's journey out of Sonora into New Mexico (J1)
note: A pregnant wolf comes up out of the Sonoran mountains alone, crosses the Bavispe and walks north towards the line and the Animas country.
label: She-wolf, out of Sonora
credit: Traced from a Mexican wolf photograph, US Fish and Wildlife Service (public domain)
reasoning: She stands for her whole journey north; the drawing sits at her crossing of the Bavispe.

name: A steel trap with the drag
stands_for: Billy's trapline in the Peloncillos (J1 and J2)
note: Billy and his father wax their traps and set them along the trails of the Peloncillos, each on a chain that ends in a two-pronged drag buried with it.
label: Newhouse No. 4½ wolf trap
credit: Drawn after Newhouse trap catalogue engravings, 1890s-1919 (public domain)

name: The boundary obelisk
stands_for: The white boundary monuments along 31°20′ N
note: From the red hills south of the line Billy sees one of the white boundary obelisks standing alone in the desert to the east.
label: Boundary monument, 1890s line
credit: Drawn after the International Boundary Commission's monument photographs, 1892-94 (public domain)

name: The cockpit at the hacienda
stands_for: The hacienda where the wolf is made to fight (J2)
note: At a hacienda by a river near Colonia Morelos the wolf is taken from Billy and put in a pit to fight dogs at the fair.
label: Cockpit at the hacienda fair
credit: Drawn; the wolf is the traced she-wolf (US Fish and Wildlife Service photograph, public domain)

name: The ruined church
stands_for: The hermit's ruined church at Huisiachepic (J3)
note: In a ruined, nearly empty town on the upper Bavispe Billy meets an old man living in the broken church, who tells him a long tale.
label: Ruined adobe church, upper Bavispe
credit: Drawn after photographs of the Quarai mission ruin by suemruth (CC BY 2.0) and of Mission San Juan Capistrano about 1900, California Historical Society (public domain)

name: Paquimé's mud walls
stands_for: The ruins of Paquimé, beside Casas Grandes
note: The brothers ride past the old adobe ruins of Paquimé on their way into Casas Grandes.
label: Paquimé, adobe ruins, 1940s
credit: Drawn after photographs by Gary Lee Todd and DiSchamelrider (CC0)

name: The San Diego house front, L. T.
stands_for: The Hacienda de San Diego, Luis Terrazas's house (J4, J5)
note: The brothers and the girl ride up to the hacienda of San Diego, whose house front carries its name in an arch over the initials of the old owner.
label: Hacienda de San Diego, Terrazas house
credit: Drawn from the book's description; no reusable photograph found

name: The opera caravan with its gilt
stands_for: The stranded opera troupe on the Madera road (J4)
note: South of Las Varas the brothers come on the travelling opera company again, its gaudy caravan wagons halted in a field beside the road.
label: Travelling opera wagons, 1940s
credit: Drawn from the book's description; wagon form after circus wagon photographs, c. 1900-25 (public domain, CC0)

name: The blind man with his cane
stands_for: The blind man's house north of San José (J4)
note: Billy, alone, follows a light at dusk to a lone house where a blind man and his wife take him in and the man tells of his life.
label: Blind man of the revolution
credit: Drawn; hat and coat after a Fortepan photograph of a peasant with a cane (Fortepan 28839, CC BY-SA 3.0). This drawing is shared under CC BY-SA 3.0

name: The red Waco plane
stands_for: The red plane over the Babícora lake country (J7)
note: On the road towards La Boquilla Billy watches a big red Waco plane come in from the west, circle and come down beyond the lake.
label: Red Waco cabin biplane, 1930s
credit: Drawn after photographs of a Waco YKS-6 by RuthAS (CC BY 3.0) and a Waco UEC by Armchair Aviator (CC BY 2.0)

name: The gypsies' wrecked airplane
stands_for: The gypsies hauling an old airplane north on the river trail (J7)
note: On the river trail north of Corralitos Billy falls in with gypsies who are hauling the bones of an old airplane north on a cart.
label: Gypsies' airplane, lost in 1915
credit: Drawn; fuselage after a Curtiss JN-4B 3-view by Kaboldy (CC BY-SA 3.0), oxen after Giovanni Fattori's etching (CC0). This drawing is shared under CC BY-SA 3.0

name: The crippled dog
stands_for: The ruined waystation by the highway east of the Black Range (J7)
note: Sheltering from the rain in three ruined adobes by the highway, Billy drives off an old crippled dog that comes in at the door.
label: Old dog at the roadside ruin
credit: The traced she-wolf outline (US Fish and Wildlife Service, public domain), bent; the ruin drawn

name: The Trinity cloud
stands_for: The false dawn, read as the Trinity test of 16 July 1945 (J7)
note: Before daybreak Billy is woken by a great white light that floods the country and then dies away, long before the real dawn. Readers take it for the first atomic bomb, tested at the Trinity Site on 16 July 1945.
label: Trinity test, 16 July 1945
credit: Cap traced from the Trinity test photograph, US government, 1945 (public domain)
reasoning: The book names no place or event for the light. The drawing stands on the Trinity Site itself (Wikidata Q19842077), in the empty Jornada del Muerto, at the far end of the direction the dotted false-dawn line points from the waystation.

name: The brothers and "the girl" riding south
stands_for: The brothers' ride south from San Diego with "the girl" (J4)
note: Billy and Boyd ride south from San Diego towards Las Varas, with "the girl" riding double behind Boyd on his horse.
credit: Horse and rider traced from Eadweard Muybridge, Animal Locomotion plate 580, 1887 (public domain), drawn twice; "the girl" and the hats drawn
reasoning: A character vignette on the long, empty stretch of the J4 leg from Mata Ortiz to the opera camp (3-01). The point is on the route line (data/journeys.geojson, j4-seg-20, 85% along); the ref is the leg's first stop. Placed to the west so it clears the steers and the blind man's house.

name: Boyd and "the girl"
stands_for: Boyd and "the girl" gone from San Diego, as Billy later hears it (J6)
note: One morning Billy wakes at San Diego to find Boyd and "the girl" gone together, and he never sees them ride again.
credit: Horse and rider traced from Eadweard Muybridge, Animal Locomotion plate 580, 1887 (public domain), drawn twice; Boyd's straw hat and "the girl" drawn
reasoning: A character vignette on the reported J6 leg from San Diego towards Namiquipa (3-14), on the route line (j6-seg-03, 25% along); the ref is the leg's first stop. J6 is told, not seen, so the drawing shows the pair as Billy pictures them.

name: Billy alone, searching
stands_for: Billy's weeks of searching for Boyd across Chihuahua (J5)
note: Billy rides south alone in grey weather with the shotgun across his saddle, looking for Boyd for weeks and finding only rumour.
credit: Horse and rider traced from Eadweard Muybridge, Animal Locomotion plate 580, 1887 (public domain); the hat and shotgun drawn
reasoning: A character vignette on the long J5 leg from San Diego to Cuauhtémoc (3-14), on the route line (j5-seg-13, 60% along); the ref is the nearer end of the leg.

name: Billy riding north in the rain
stands_for: Billy's ride north to San Buenaventura (J7)
note: Under a grey sky Billy rides north all day on a wet horse through the mud of the upland roads, the rain blowing over his slicker.
credit: Horse and rider traced from Eadweard Muybridge, Animal Locomotion plate 580, 1887 (public domain), mirrored; the slicker, the hat and the rain drawn
reasoning: A character vignette on the J7 leg from Quijada's cabin to San Buenaventura (4-06), on the route line (j7-seg-37, 50% along); the ref is the leg's end. South-west keeps it off Álamo and Boyd's grave.

name: The travois with Boyd's bones
stands_for: Billy taking his brother's remains north to the border (J7)
note: Billy rides north along the river for three days with his brother's remains lashed on a travois of sapling poles dragging behind the horse.
label: North with Boyd's bones
credit: Horse and rider traced from Eadweard Muybridge, Animal Locomotion plate 580, 1887 (public domain); the travois drawn after a photograph of a man on a mule travois, about 1876, Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument (public domain)
reasoning: A character vignette on the J7 leg from the gypsies' camp to the border west of Dog Springs (4-08), on the route line (j7-seg-43, 50% along); the ref is the leg's end. The label is there because a travois is not obvious at map size.

name: The windmill and the stone tank
stands_for: The windmill tank on the high prairie (J4)
note: At evening the brothers water Niño and Bailey at a trough of hewn limestone under a turning windmill, whose vanes throw a long shadow over the prairie.
label: Windmill and stone tank
credit: Drawn after a photograph of an Aermotor windmill in New Mexico by SteveStrummer (CC0) and an Aermotor advertisement of 1895 (public domain)
reasoning: The book gives the tank no place; it falls between Quijada's remuda and Boquilla (3-05 sits between 3-04 and 3-06). The point is on the J4 route line there (j4-seg-29, 40% along); the ref is the nearer stop.

name: Corriente steers on the Boquilla road
stands_for: The steer herd on the road to Boquilla (J4)
note: On the road to Boquilla the brothers meet vaqueros trailing a thousand wild corriente steers from the south of the Babícora up towards the pens at Naco.
label: Corriente steers, bound for Naco
credit: Drawn after photographs of longhorn steers by Carol M. Highsmith (public domain) and Clinton and Charles Robertson (CC BY 2.0)
reasoning: North of the pin, so it clears the red plane to the south-east.

name: Sandhill cranes going south
stands_for: The cranes over the river camp south of Mata Ortiz (J5)
note: Camped on a gravel bar in the river with "the girl", Billy watches the cranes pass south high overhead in the night.
label: Sandhill cranes going south
credit: Drawn after a photograph of sandhill cranes in flight, US Fish and Wildlife Service (public domain)
reasoning: West of the pin, away from the road north to Mata Ortiz. The cranes come back in 3-13, 4-06 and 4-08.

name: The cottonwood camp on the river
stands_for: The river camp near San José where Boyd is shot (J4)
note: Near San José the brothers make camp under the river cottonwoods and swim at night; at dawn riders on the far bank shoot Boyd.
label: Cottonwood camp on the river
credit: Drawn
reasoning: East of the pin, so it clears the truck and the blind man's house to the west.

name: The farmworkers' truck
stands_for: The truck that carries the wounded Boyd away (J4, J6)
note: Billy flags down an old flatbed truck full of farmworkers on the dirt road, and they lift the wounded Boyd into its bed and drive him away.
label: Farmworkers' flatbed truck
credit: Drawn after a photograph of a 1930 Ford Model AA truck by Alf van Beem (CC0)
reasoning: From zoom 10 only: at lower zooms it would crowd the cottonwood camp and the blind man's house.

name: Boyd's grave on the Gallego road
stands_for: Boyd's grave at San Buenaventura (J7)
note: In the walled burial ground above San Buenaventura Billy lifts the board cross from his brother's cairn and digs all day and into the night.
label: Boyd's grave, Gallego road
credit: Drawn from the book's description
reasoning: East of the pin, away from the town.

name: The fair at Madera
stands_for: The April fair in the mountain town of Madera (J7)
note: In late April Billy walks through a fair beyond the railway at Madera, under strung lights, in air smelling of pine smoke and the sawmill.
label: Madera fair, late April
credit: Drawn
reasoning: South-west of the pin, away from the opera camp to the north-east.
